Antruly/libuvcpp.description: The core objective of libuvcpp is to improve development efficiency in C++ environments while preserving libuv's high performance and original semantics. It systematically encapsulates libuv's fundamental types into corresponding C++ classes and consolidates related methods into appropriate classes, making the interface more aligned with C++ conventions, making everyday development more convenient, and enhancing code readability. Building on this foundation, libuvcpp also extends modules such as memory pools, Net, Web, and SSL, providing commonly used tools and services in mainstream development, helping developers quickly build and develop projects.
Antruly/libuvcpp.body:
# libuvcpp

🔧 Modern C++11 wrapper for [libuv](https://github.com/libuv/libuv) — event-driven I/O with
object-oriented APIs, dual-mode async/sync support, HTTP/1.1, WebSocket (RFC 6455), and SSL/TLS.

- **Version**: `1.2.7-dev` — **Author**: `zhuweiye` — **License**: `MIT`
- **Languages**: [English](https://github.com/Antruly/libuvcpp/blob/HEAD/README.md) · [中文](https://github.com/Antruly/libuvcpp/blob/HEAD/README.zh.md)

---

## Overview

libuvcpp provides a thin, idiomatic C++ layer over libuv's event loop, handles, and requests.
It preserves libuv's performance while adding RAII resource management, `std::function` callbacks,
and higher-level client/server abstractions for TCP, UDP, HTTP, and WebSocket.

The library is organized into layered modules:

```
application
┌────────────┐
│ web (HTTP/WS) │  ← uvcpp_http_client/server, uvcpp_ws_client/server
├────────────┤
│ http2        │  ← h2 session/connection layers, nghttp2 glue (`UVCPP_ENABLE_NGHTTP2=ON`)
├────────────┤
│ ssl (TLS)    │  ← uvcpp_ssl, uvcpp_ssl_context (OpenSSL wrapper)
├────────────┤
│ net          │  ← uvcpp_tcp_client/server, uvcpp_udp_client/server
├────────────┤
│ handle + req │  ← uvcpp_loop, uvcpp_tcp,…
```

Baskerville42/outage-data-ua.body:
# outage-data-ua

Public repository and tools for automatic collection, parsing, visualization (HTML) and automatic generation of PNG images of graphs of planned/emergency power outages in Ukraine.

The project collects data from open web pages of suppliers and stores them in JSON 'as is' in the `data/` directory. These data are then displayed in a fixed HTML template and converted to PNG images, which are stored in `images/<region>/gpv-x-x.png`.

---

## Data Format
Each region is stored in a file `data/<region>.json`. Basic structure (abbreviated):

```json
{
  "regionId": "kyiv",
  "regionAffiliation": "м. Київ",
  "lastUpdated": "2025-11-06T11:41:56.430Z",
  "fact": { "updateFact": "06.11.2025 09:09" },
  "preset": { "updateFact": "04.11.2025 18:00" },
  "lastUpdateStatus": { "status": "parsed", "ok": true, "code": 200, "message": null, "at": "2025-11-06T11:41:56.430Z", "attempt": 5 },
  "meta": { "schemaVersion": "1.0.0", "contentHash": "..." }
}
```

- `preset` — planned outages for the week for each group (weekly template). Stored 'as is' without structure normalization.
- `fact` — actual/emergency outages for today and tomorrow for each group. Also...

RixyPow/netzapret.description: Traffic dispatcher for Windows: flexible configuration of blocking and VPN binding for each domain.
RixyPow/netzapret.body:
# NetZapret

Traffic dispatcher for Windows. For each application, domain, or subnet, it decides where to route traffic: **through desync** (Zapret / winws2), **through VPN** (sing-box), or **directly** — and runs both engines under unified supervision.

Replaces the Zapret + VPN-client combination and does what neither of them can do separately: **applies VPN selectively, without breaking desync for everything else.**

## Installation

1. Download the archive from the [releases](https://github.com/RixyPow/netzapret/releases/latest) page.
2. Extract anywhere.
3. Run `NetZapret.exe`.

No need to install anything else — neither .NET, nor sing-box, nor Zapret: everything is included. The program will request administrator rights on its own; without them, neither the tunnel nor the packet capture driver will start.

You'll only need a **VPN subscription link** — any provider is supported, including VLESS, Trojan, Hysteria2, and Shadowsocks. It's entered in the «VPN» section.

The link is equivalent to a password: it provides access to the full list of servers with credentials. It's stored next to the program in `config\netzapret.json` and is never sent anywhere.

Whalica/OJ_Insight.body:
# OJ Insight

**Organize training records scattered across multiple Online Judges into a single trustworthy, clear, and long-term trackable personal profile.**

OJ Insight is a cross-platform training data dashboard for algorithmic competition participants. Currently supports Codeforces, AtCoder, Luogu, Niuke, QOJ, and LeetCode, and provides an independent ICPC / CCPC Tracker. All data is saved locally, and the application clearly distinguishes between per-problem AC records, publicly available summaries, and missing data, avoiding assembling incomparable statistics that look "complete".

[Download latest version](https://github.com/Whalica/OJ_Insight/releases/latest) · [View release notes](https://github.com/Whalica/OJ_Insight/blob/HEAD/docs/UPDATEINFO.md) · [Report issues](https://github.com/Whalica/OJ_Insight/issues) · [Build from source](https://github.com/Whalica/OJ_Insight/blob/HEAD/docs/BUILDING.md)

Current version: **v0.9.2**, supporting Windows, MacOS, and Linux.

## Why Use OJ Insight

### View Six OJs on One Dashboard

No need to open multiple personal homepages separately. OJ Insight consolidates accounts, training activities, problem-solving counts, difficulty distributions, and rating changes from different platforms, and supports configuring multiple accounts on the same platform.

### Comprehensive Statistics Without Sacrificing Accuracy

Different OJs expose different data. OJ Insight distinguishes between:

- Verifiable per-problem AC records;
- Activity dates or problem count summaries provided only by the platform;
- Data that is temporarily unavailable.

It won't fabricate submissions when per-problem history is missing, and ratings and difficulty won't be forcibly converted across platforms. Failed synchronization only updates the error status, and previously cached data remains accessible.

### Extending from Daily Training to ICPC / CCPC Problem Review

The ICPC / CCPC Tracker aggregates ICPC, CCPC, and provincial competition problem sets, and can be filtered by year, stage, competition site, series, and completion progress. Problem completion status comes from local QOJ records, and difficulty levels (gold, silver, bronze, iron) are displayed when public rankings are available.

### Send a Contest Directly to an LLM for Review

"Contest Review" can collect problems, the entire submission timeline, judging results, and available historical code by OJ, account, and contest ID, generating a fixed-structure ZIP. After uploading the review package to an LLM, no explanation is needed; if the chat interface prompts for input, just say "start review". Currently supports Codeforces and AtCoder first, with other OJs showing clear integration status on the page.

# University Physics Experiment Reports

Reports and LaTeX templates for University Physics experiments at Zhejiang University. [Browse experiments](https://github.com/YuNa-Zju/phy_exp/blob/HEAD/experiments/README.md) · [Download PDF reports](https://github.com/YuNa-Zju/phy_exp/releases/latest)

## Getting Started

Install Python 3.10+ and TeX Live (Windows / Linux) or MacTeX (macOS). On GitHub, click **Code → Download ZIP**, then extract and open the project folder. Open a terminal at the level containing `README.md` and run the commands below. On Windows, you can replace `python3` with `python`.

### Create New Report

```bash
python3 scripts/new_experiment.py "单摆法测量重力加速度"
```

Open the generated `experiments/单摆法测量重力加速度/report.tex` and fill in as prompted. Running the command again for the same experiment will successively generate `report-02.tex`, `report-03.tex`; if multiple reports already exist, it creates the next one after the highest number.

For preview reports, add `--preview` at the end of the command:

```bash
python3 scripts/new_experiment.py "单摆法测量重力加速度" --preview
```

Place images in the experiment's `figures/` folder: use `diagrams/` for principle diagrams, `plots/` for result figures, and `photos/` for photographs. Filenames can include the report number, for example `原始数据-02.jpg`.

### Generate PDF

```bash
python3 scripts/build_reports.py "experiments/单摆法测量重力加速度/report.tex"
```

The generated PDF is located at `build/reports/单摆法测量重力加速度/`. When compiling other versions, replace `report.tex` in the command with the corresponding filename.

## Common LaTeX Syntax

The complete [report template](https://github.com/YuNa-Zju/phy_exp/blob/HEAD/templates/report.tex) is automatically copied by the creation script. The code below can be placed directly in the report body.

### Units and Formulas

```tex
\SI{10}{mA}                                % numbers and units
\si{\meter\per\second}                     % units only: meters per second
\si{\degreeCelsius}…
```

chinjiaqing/jc-daily-report.body:
# ⚽ Football Signal Radar · Daily Signal Report

> **Disregard emotion, focus only on signals.**
> Three-channel odds movement cross-verification, no action on low odds, no entry without clear signals; automatic execution before match, automatic settlement after match.

## 🚀 Online Site

- **[https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/](https://chinjiaqing.github.io/jc-daily-report/)**
- Auto-updates every hour, historical dates archived, review anytime
- Covers **500~1300+** daily matches (full coverage of sports lottery/Asian odds), auto-marks signals and bets

---

## The Detours We've Avoided

Tried **models** — piled up parameters everywhere, but looking back, the model just re-read what the market had already priced, and no amount of parameters could generate anything new.

Tried **studying house tactics** — staring at the bookmaker's methods, guessing endlessly, the more you guess the more it resembles paranoia. Finally understood: guessing the house's moves is not as good as watching the price.

Also tried **AI predictions** — injuries, team morale, form, each point sounds perfectly logical, but all are already priced into the odds. No matter how convincingly presented, the market doesn't buy it.

After taking these detours, one simple truth remains:

> **Follow the money, the odds will speak.**
> But when humans read the odds, they easily get emotional — chasing favorites, fearing underdogs, shaky hands at game time, it's obvious at a glance that emotion is driving the trading.

So we hand both 'reading' and 'buying' to machines, leaving humans with just one thing: **discipline**.

## Three Informants, One Referee

**European odds** monitor market-wide odds movements — who is being collectively abandoned, who is quietly supporting the line, whether the draw defense has been given up. This is the closest informant.

**Asian odds** monitor the spread and water level — sudden in-game pivots, upper side fund sniping, money speaks louder than words.

**Over/Under** monitor the line — once a goal-scoring environment emerges, the match's goal count is usually predetermined.

The three informants each have their own signals, and only when they align does the referee make the call; **skip matches where they don't align (European and Asian odds conflict)** — if the informants are arguing with each other, why place a bet.

## Discipline Matters More Than Insight

Once direction is set, everything else is discipline:

- **Don't act on low odds** — single bets under 1.5 odds, multiple bets under 1.3 after folding, no matter how good the signal, don't buy. At those odds, winning doesn't make money anyway
- **No unclear signals** — no signal, conflicting signals, unclear direction, observe all. Missing an opportunity doesn't lose money, buying wrong does
- **Quality determines position size** — stronger signals mean larger stakes (1/2/4 units), no all-in bets
- **Auto-bet 15 minutes before match, auto-settle after result** — no in-game hand tremors, no urge to add stakes after winning or chase losses

---

## ⚠️ Disclaimer

This project is for data research only and does not constitute any purchase advice. Lottery tickets should be purchased at offline retail stores; participants must be 18 years or older.

leizongmin/ZeroWeb.body:
# ZeroWeb

ZeroWeb is an experimental cross-platform browser project written in Rust. This repository is doing two things at the same time:

Official website: [zeroweb.leizm.com](https://zeroweb.leizm.com)

- An embeddable and reusable `ZeroWebView` library
- A complete `ZeroBrowser` browser application

The main line of the project will try to keep the core code and dependency boundaries in its own hands, so the page kernel is mainly built up gradually from Rust components with permissive licenses. DOM, CSS, layout, rendering, navigation, and security boundaries are all supplemented layer by layer in this repository.

This is also an AI-first engineering experiment: people are only responsible for solution design, critical decisions, and result verification, while code development is almost entirely completed autonomously by AI. We want to see how far AI can push such a complex system, given that architecture boundaries, testing, and acceptance are all clearly documented.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> This repository is still in the experimental stage, mainly for learning, research, and engineering exploration. The core crates and tests already have a lot of content, but the browser shell, complete page JavaScript runtime, and real site compatibility are still in progress. It is not a daily-use browser right now. For commercial or other production use, please evaluate the risks of functionality, security, compatibility, performance, and license boundaries yourself.

**Quick Navigation**

- [Roadmap](https://github.com/leizongmin/ZeroWeb/blob/HEAD/ROADMAP.md)
- [Official Website](https://zeroweb.leizm.com)
- [Current Status](#current-status)
- [Quick Start](#quick-start)
- [Repository Structure](#repository-structure)
- [Documentation Navigation](#documentation-navigation)
- [Contributing](#contributing)
- [License](#license)

## Project Positioning

- **Embedding-first**: In addition to browser applications, the project also needs to deliver a stable Rust `ZeroWebView` API for easy integration by other applications.
- **License boundary first**: The main line dependencies prioritize permissive licenses like MIT, Apache-2.0, and BSD to avoid core capabilities being constrained by unsuitable copyleft dependencies.
- **Full-stack Rust route**: The page kernel, host layer, and rendering infrastructure are all completed as much as possible within the Rust ecosystem.
- **AI can write, but must be reviewable**: AI-assisted contributions are welcome, but the changes submitted must be clearly explained, thoroughly tested, and clearly reviewed.

michaelChe956/Cadence-skills.body:
# Cadence

## Project Overview

Cadence is an Agent Skills collaboration system for five endpoints: Claude Code, pi, Codex, Kimi Code, and omp (oh-my-pi). It organizes work such as requirement clarification, design, planning, implementation, testing, review, and debugging into reusable Skills, and provides Schema 4.0 KnowledgeBase capabilities for Java and Vue/React legacy projects.

The current `cadence-init` plugin version in this repository is `0.0.4`. Cadence installation, updates, and uninstallation are managed by `install.sh` in the repository root; Skills use Git repositories as sources and are consumed by different Agents through three-tier skill-level symlinks, without relying on plugin marketplace registration.

## How It Works

Cadence Skills are automatically triggered based on task intent, and can also be manually invoked using bare Skill names. A typical workflow is as follows:

1. Use `/pre-check` to check basic tools and environment.
2. Use `/mcp-configuration` to configure project MCP (must be before `rule-config`——the latter's permission block depends on `.mcp.json` being in place).
3. Use `/rule-config` to configure project rules, `cadence/` artifact directory, and OpenSpec collaboration entry point; use `/project-rules-examples` as needed to complete personalized rule templates.
4. After filling in Schema 4.0 input for legacy projects, use `/knowledge-base-bootstrap` to initialize KnowledgeBase.
5. Before requirements, design, planning, coding, testing, review, or debugging, use `/knowledge-base-context` to retrieve minimal task context.
6. When project facts change, prepare a complete change package and use `/knowledge-base-update` to incrementally update the knowledge base.

KnowledgeBase Skills only read evidence within the authorization scope of the target project; they do not replace business code, database migrations, deployment, or release processes.

## Five-Endpoint Nightly Verification Status (`eval/`)

End-to-end verification is performed using containerized nightly tests outside of CI: one fresh container per endpoint (install CLI → authenticate → install.sh → four commands → probe → score to disk → destroy). First night baseline (2026-09-08/09, 2 rounds per endpoint):

# Glitch Studio (⚠️Under Development!!!)

Glitch Studio is a web application that enables real-time image and video processing and editing through a node-based editor, and can also be used as a shader playground.

- All image processing is performed on the GPU for high efficiency
- Resolution-independent so rendering at any resolution produces consistent results without visual changes (※1)
- FPS-independent so rendering at any frame rate produces consistent results without changes in motion speed
- Aspect-ratio-independent so rendering at any aspect ratio produces consistent results without distortion (※2)
- Expressions can be interpreted as [AiScript](https://aiscript-dev.github.io/ja/)
- UI thread, audio processing thread, and image processing thread are separated, allowing efficient use of multi-core and fast operation

With the right idea, you can create various things. The possibilities are infinite.

## Concept

A mechanism where various "nodes" are wired together to process data.

Nodes are like functions - they receive input (though some don't) and return output.

"Data" is not limited to images - it can be scalar fields or vector fields. In other words, any data that is a two-dimensional array containing values of some type is a subject of calculation (processing). In that sense, it could also be called GPGPU.

That said, what is ultimately output is an image (video).

In Glitch Studio, we intentionally allow connecting different types of outputs and inputs (there is also an option for strict type checking).

Something interesting might happen.

---

- (※1) Some exceptions exist (such as Pixel sort, some effects that focus on individual pixels)
- (※2) Some exceptions exist

# Mineradio - LX Music / MR

> A secondary development and long-term maintenance project of an immersive desktop music player based on Electron.
> Continuous iteration around music playback, lyrics, visualization, local network control, resource stability, and AI Agent.

[**Windows Download**](https://github.com/ww085213/Mineradio-LX-Music/releases/download/v1.6.1/Mineradio.Setup.1.6.1.exe) · [**GitHub Release**](https://github.com/ww085213/Mineradio-LX-Music/releases/tag/v1.6.1) · [**Douyin Project Demo**](https://v.douyin.com/eRlkIQrTOTw/)

## Project Overview

### Main Interface

Immersive homepage display: daily recommendations, recent playback, platform charts, playlist plaza, music radio, local network remote control, and real-time spectrum features.

### AI Agent "XiaoM"

XiaoM is not just a chat window; it can convert natural language commands into actual player operations, such as searching and playing songs, adjusting volume, switching audio quality, managing playlists, and more.

### Lyrics and Visualization

Particle visualization, bilingual lyrics, and real-time spectrum combined display, showcasing the immersive visual capabilities of the desktop music player.

> Screenshots are from the actual running interface of the current version; the project is continuously iterating.

## Project Highlights

- **Complete desktop application experience**: local music, online search, playlists, charts, radio, lyrics, playback queue, system tray, and media controls.
- **AI Agent "XiaoM"**: Support for controlling playback, queue, playlists, volume, audio quality, lyrics animation, interface, and visual effects through natural language.
- **Multiple lyrics and visualization capabilities**: translated lyrics, desktop lyrics, real-time spectrum, particle visualization, 3D lyrics stage, custom wallpapers and video backgrounds.
- **Local network multi-device remote control**: Support for controlling the desktop player within the same network after scanning with a mobile device.
- **Playback stability optimization**: Continuous optimization around resource resolution, caching, next track prefetching, timeout, failure retry, and fallback mechanisms.
- **Long list and interface performance optimization**: Batch rendering and interaction optimization for large amounts of songs, playlists, and complex interfaces.
- **Complete release process**: Building Windows installer packages using Electron / electron-builder and releasing versions through GitHub Release.
- **Real user feedback-driven iteration**: Continuously showcasing project features and version updates through [Douyin project demo](https://v.douyin.com/eRlkIQrTOTw/), with related accounts accumulating **9000+ followers**, continuously improving features based on actual feedback.

**Simplified Chinese** · [English](https://github.com/yzddmr6/PrismSpace/blob/HEAD/README.en.md) # PrismSpace · Prism Space **Based on Android work profile, lightweight native app dual-open solution**

PrismSpace creates truly isolated dual-open spaces at the system level—app data, accounts, and storage are completely separate, with better compatibility and no additional performance overhead. Implemented based on Android's native work profile capability, different from virtualization solutions like Parallel Space. Supports three operating modes: Normal, Shizuku, and Root.
Home: Space status and main operations Space: Main space/dual-open space app list Operation panel: Launch, freeze, uninstall
## ✨ Features 🔒 **System-level Isolation** — Based on Android managed profile, the main space and dual-open space are two independent system user environments, with data invisible to each other, not in-process virtualization. 📦 **Use Without Root** — Normal mode has zero barriers to entry, creating spaces, cloning apps, managing clones, and transferring files are all available. Root and Shizuku are optional enhancements. ⚙️ **Complete App Management** — Clone, launch, freeze, unfreeze, and uninstall app clones, automatically handle multi-module installation packages, one-stop management of dual-open apps. 📂 **Cross-Space File Transfer** — Transfer files between the main space and dual-open space through the system sharing panel, with the system save panel writing to the target space. ⚡ **Lightweight and Native** — Apps run directly in system-level profiles, with no virtualization runtime overhead, and compatibility identical to native installation. ## 🚀 Quick Start 1. Download the APK from [Releases](https://github.com/yzddmr6/PrismSpace/releases) and install it. 2. Open PrismSpace and follow the guide to create a dual-open space (Android work profile process). 3. On the 'Space' page, select the app you want to clone from the main space. 4. In normal mode, the complete installation package will sync to the dual-open space; click install and confirm in 'Prism-Dual-Open Space'. ...
